notes: Phobos Agriculture crops (Agriculture 0.40.0): what a Firstlight rack grows, what each planting needs and what a harvest gives. One entry per crop; the entry's name is what a saved planting stores, so a published crop is frozen (frozen-crops.json): change one by adding a crop beside it. Every crop conserves mass: water + nutrient + 0.4 x carbon - vapour = final - seed, where 0.4 x carbon is the carbon dioxide taken in less the oxygen given off (CH2O, 30 g per mol of carbon). Growth times are authored gameplay balance, far shorter than real cultivation; see docs/development/agriculture-research.md for the NASA and ESA sources and their limits. The items section names the crop items the code builds from the materials pack, their text and what eating one gives.

potato.notes: Seed potato into a five-kilogram cohort over 96 hours at 0.75 kW. A harvest keeps one seed potato and gives 0.4 kg raw portions for the Hearth-2. Unchanged since Agriculture 0.2.0.

lettuce.notes: One seed packet into 1.2 kg of lettuce over 48 hours at 0.4 kW, cut as 0.25 kg portions eaten as they are. Unchanged since Agriculture 0.2.0.

lettuce-seed.notes: Lettuce left to bolt for seed: one packet into four packets over 96 hours. An authored seed cycle, separate from the food crop.

wheat.notes: Dwarf wheat (Agriculture 0.41.0): one 50 g packet of seed wheat into a 1.4 kg cohort over 84 hours at 1.2 kW. A harvest keeps one packet back for the next planting and gives one 0.4 kg portion of grain; the rest, about 0.95 kg, is straw. Authored in the ratios NASA Kennedy Space Center's Biomass Production Chamber found against potato: a slightly shorter cycle (77 to 86 days against 90 to 105), the most light, about 30 to 40% of the plant edible, and a ripe crop that is mostly dry matter. See docs/development/agriculture-crop-expansion.md; the hours are authored gameplay balance.

PhobosVerdemorrowHearthFlatbread.notes: The game's own prepared-meal values (food 9, satiety 5): a loaf from 0.4 kg of grain is about four potato portions of food energy.
